causalModel.founding: The Xit-Xaht went on cutting stone after the Duskfall told every tribe to stop, on the order of a Hist they had bound with sap.
causalModel.siteAdvantages: A firm rock shelf at the end of an upland ridge, 68 m by 42 m of buildable ground with the block face in its own southern lip. A headwater stream along that lip serves for mortar and slaking. The east side falls away in a 55 m escarpment that no neighbour climbs uninvited.
causalModel.occupantsMotive: Tsono-Xuhil has not woken. The Amber Plasm seep has resumed and the conduits carry it up the escarpment into the works. The courses have started rising again.
causalModel.pressures: Labour. Every course needs hands the tribe does not have, so the pens fill from the neighbouring villages; the shelf is also too small for what the shaper has drawn.
causalModel.wouldChangeIf: The conduits were cut, or another tribe accepted the invitation to help.

candidates.why: The rock shelf at the ridge end: 68 m x 42 m of ground between 198.3 m and 209 m, falling ~8.5 m north to south in three readable steps, flood band 0, 4.1 m above the water table, a headwater stream along its southern lip and a 55 m escarpment on the east. 85 m from Tsono-Xuhil and 296 m from the Gideon-Stormhold road. Every parcel measured on this ground fits the slope ladder at plinth, pad or dug-in; none needs a graded pad over 2 m.
The plotted position, 115 m south. Slope 46.9 deg at the point and Δ 24.0 m across a 30 x 20 m core; nothing above the smallest prop can stand on it.
candidates.rejectedBecause: Δ ≥ 2 m over every candidate footprint. The ladder forbids grading there. Re-sited, not graded.

candidates.why: The gorge floor at the Hist's own feet, 148 m, on the river. It would put the works around the tree as the lore describes.
candidates.rejectedBecause: Water depth 0.1 m, height above the water table -0.12 m and river band 1: the floor is the channel. A stone works cannot stand in it. The flat ground within 170 m is 6.5 m of relief at best.

districts.notes: The upper step, 205-209 m. Mud shells and a tent for the taken labourers, who are not Xit-Xaht and are not permitted stone. The step below holds the works, so the overseers there look straight down into the pens.

The middle step, 198-206 m. The half-built quarter: courses, frontage dais, statue court, watch column and the conduit head at the eastern lip. Every course runs along the riser of the step. Ayleid-set blocks, spans and stairs carry the terracing; the xanmeer pillars carry the conduit head. The two authors' pieces stand in separate parcels and never abut.

The lower step and the stream lip, 190-203 m. Block face, kiln, scaffold staging and the haul gate. The stockade scaffold family is placed per its own snap logic: matched base and top side counts, bridges between decks, ramps and stairs to climb.
